# Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0

## 1. Application

This version applies to tickets opened on or after 2026-04-01 00:00 CT. The version is chosen by the ticket's **open time in Central
Time**, and nothing else. A ticket keeps its version for its whole life, including credits, cap
and claim window, even if it is restored, claimed or decided after another version takes effect.
The UTC date of the open time, the restoration date and the claim date do not change the version."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":2,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.1 **Time zone.** All service-level times, business hours, deadlines and calendar dates are in US
Central Time (America/Chicago), written "CT". Central Standard Time is UTC−06:00 and Central
Daylight Time is UTC−05:00. CDT applied from 2025-03-09 to 2025-11-02, and from 2026-03-08. A
timestamp recorded in another zone (for example Eastern Daylight Time, UTC−04:00, or UTC in system
logs) is converted to CT before anything is measured. "Date" (the restoration date, the claim date
or a notice date) means the CT calendar date of the timestamp after conversion.

2.2 **Business hours** are 08:00 to 18:00 CT, Monday to Friday, except Northstar holidays (see the
Northstar holiday calendar). A business day is a Monday-to-Friday date that is not a Northstar
holiday. Every business day has exactly 10 business hours."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a179-74a0-b361-5bbac7a91e67","seq":3,"headings":["Northstar Support Service Level Schedule v2.0","2. Definitions"],"text":"2.3 **Clocks.** Every ticket has a response clock and a restoration clock, which start together. A
24×7 clock counts all elapsed time; across a daylight-saving change it counts the actual elapsed
time. A business-hours clock counts only time inside business hours. Elapsed time is measured in

# Support Severity Guide

Northstar Support classifies severity from the business impact recorded in the ticket (its
description and notes). Test the definitions in order; the severity is the first one the recorded
impact meets.

## Severity 1: Critical

A Northstar product failure that, with **no workaround available**, either (a) stops the customer's
production or operations (a production line, a plant process, or a distribution, dispatch or
facility-operations activity cannot continue), or (b) makes NS-Cloud unavailable to **all** of the
customer's users.

## Severity 2: High

Not Severity 1, and any one of: (a) production or operations continue but are materially degraded;
(b) a control, alarming or condition-monitoring function is unavailable (not merely intermittent)
for one or more machines, lines, buildings or sites, whether or not the customer covers it with
manual checks; (c) NS-Cloud is unavailable to some, but not all, of the customer's users or sites;
(d) a Severity 1 condition with a workaround in place that needs ongoing manual effort."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a222-7410-b067-b0fda71f9451","seq":2,"headings":["Support Severity Guide","Severity 3: Medium"],"text":"Not Severity 1 or 2: a function is impaired with no reduction in production output and no loss of a
control, alarming or monitoring function (intermittent faults with backfilled data, slow
performance, a failing report, a single-user error).

## Severity 4: Low

A question, how-to, documentation issue, cosmetic defect or enhancement request, with no effect on
operations.

## Who decides

The customer's reported priority (P1 to P4) is only the customer's view: it does not set the
severity and has no effect on targets, credits or escalations. Northstar may correct the severity
up or down at any time. If the impact recorded at opening meets a different severity, that severity
governs from the open time, with its clock, targets, credits and escalations. If the impact changes
after opening, the ticket is reclassified at the moment the change is recorded."}],"total":2}

# Support Escalation Procedure

tied to the response on the response clock, deadlines tied to restoration on the restoration clock

message recorded in the ticket. Thresholds use the restoration target of the ticket's schedule
version."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a1ab-7941-b30a-7e9afd3fccd9","seq":2,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Severity 1"],"text":"1. Engage the **Support Escalation Manager** as incident lead no later than 15 minutes after clock
   start.
2. Notify the **account owner** (as recorded in Northstar CRM) no later than 30 minutes after clock
   start.
3. If the ticket is not restored when 50% of the restoration target has elapsed, notify the
   **Director of Customer Support** no later than that moment.
4. If the ticket is not restored when 100% of the restoration target has elapsed, notify the
   **VP Sales** no later than that moment, and, for a **Strategic** account (CRM account tier), the
   **Chief Revenue Officer** as well.

## Severity 2

1. If there has been no initial response when the response target elapses, notify the **Support
   Escalation Manager** no later than that moment.
2. If the ticket is not restored when the restoration target elapses, notify the **Director of
   Customer Support** and the **account owner** no later than that moment.

## Severity 3 and 4

On a Severity 3 ticket not restored when the restoration target elapses, notify the **Support
Escalation Manager** no later than that moment. Severity 4 has no escalation."},{"doc_id":"01a14c97-a1ab-7941-b30a-7e9afd3fccd9","seq":3,"headings":["Support Escalation Procedure","Tickets outside a support agreement"],"text":"A ticket is in scope only if its customer (identified by CRM account id, ERP customer id or DUNS,

**SR-39644: no service level was breached (NO_BREACH).** The true severity is Severity 2, both targets were met, no credit is owed, and no escalation or notification was triggered.

**1. The customer.** The ticket is on CRM account CRM-2048. That account carries DUNS 04-812-7730 and maps to ERP customer C-1001, Acme Mfg. Holdings, Milwaukee. It is not Acme Industrial Supply Co. (CRM-2091).

**2. Scope: in.** Acme's support terms (Schedule C) put it on the Platinum plan and name NS-Edge as a covered product. Coverage started 2025-04-01. The ticket was opened on 2026-07-23, well after that.

**3. True severity: Severity 2, not P1.** The ticket records that NS-Edge gateways stopped sending vibration data for presses 1–6 at Plant 2. The presses kept running, and technicians did manual checks every two hours. Production was not stopped, so it isn't Severity 1. The severity guide counts a lost condition-monitoring function as Severity 2 "whether or not the customer covers it with manual checks." The customer's P1 has no effect on targets.

**4. Schedule version and targets.** Service Level Schedule v2.0 applies, because the ticket opened on or after 2026-04-01 Central Time. For Severity 2 on Platinum, the targets are a 2-hour response and a 12-hour restoration, on a clock that runs around the clock. Holidays and business hours don't matter here.

**5. Clock start, pause and exclusions** (all times Central Daylight Time, UTC−05:00)
- **Clock start:** 2026-07-23 13:10, when the portal submission was received.
- **Pause:** the restoration clock paused from 2026-07-23 15:00, when the engineer asked for VPN credentials and set the ticket to Awaiting Customer. It resumed at 2026-07-24 08:30, when the customer provided them. Both ends are recorded, so 17 h 30 min is removed.
- **Exclusions:** none. The only maintenance notice on record (MN-2607) is for another customer and product. No customer-caused exclusion was asserted.

**6. Measurement**
- **Response:** the engineer's comment at 15:00 asked for access, which counts as a first response. That is 1 h 50 min against a 2-hour target, so it was **met**.
- **Restoration:** restored 2026-07-24 18:40. Total elapsed time was 29 h 30 min; minus the 17 h 30 min pause, that leaves exactly 12 h 00 min. Under schedule section 2.4, an event exactly when the target runs out counts as met, so restoration was **met with no margin**. If the pause had been one minute shorter, it would have been a breach.

**7. Credits.** None are owed, because no target was missed. No claim is on record, and none would succeed.

**8. Obligations**
- **Northstar:** nothing is owed.
  - The response-escalation trigger (notify the Support Escalation Manager) never fired, because the response came before the 15:10 deadline.
  - The restoration trigger (notify the Director of Customer Support and the account owner, Sarah Chen) would have fired at 2026-07-24 18:40, but the ticket was restored at that exact moment.
  - With no claim, there's no claim decision or credit memo. With no customer-caused exclusion asserted, no root-cause finding is due.
- **Customer:**
  - It was not required to report by phone, since that rule applies only to Severity 1. It reported through the portal, which is fine for Severity 2.
  - It did have to provide the access Northstar needed, and it met that: Kelly Ballard (Acme IT Architecture) supplied the VPN credentials, recorded 2026-07-24 08:30.
  - It has no claim to file. If it does file one, the window runs to 2026-08-23 23:59 CT, and the Director of Customer Support must decline it in writing within 30 days of receipt.
